# Phase 1b evidence cohort: what booted, what failed, what it cost

<!-- Draft (PLAN §12). The tables between findings markers are generated by
scripts/cohort_findings.py from the stored records and checked by
tests/unit/test_cohort_findings.py; never edit them by hand. The prose is
drafted from _dev_notes/cohort-run/notebook.md; the owner rewrites it. This
post stays `draft: true` until the owner publishes it. -->

Apron predicts how much GPU memory a model needs, boots it on a real GPU,
measures what vLLM actually used, runs a small task suite and a serving
benchmark, and when a boot fails, diagnoses the error, changes the plan
itself and boots it again. This post is the first cohort of real runs:
eleven models, six GPU types, one provider.

<!-- findings:headline -->
- Models measured: 11 on 6 GPU types
- Failure classes fixed and re-verified: 5 of 6
- Total cost: $9.99 of the $100 cap (failed boots included: $4.32)
<!-- /findings:headline -->

<!-- more -->

## Limits

- One measurement per point. Two repeat boots of one model bound the noise
  on one GPU type; everything else is n = 1.
- One provider: RunPod, Secure cloud. No managed endpoint is compared yet
  (that is Part 3).
- Multi-GPU appears once, in the tensor-parallel failure proof. The
  activation estimate does not fit that one point.
- The task suite is three short questions scored by exact match. It shows
  whether a model answers at all, not how good it is.
- The activation estimate below is fitted to these boots. Why vLLM's
  profiled peak tracks the output projection is not yet traced to a line of
  vLLM.
- The Mamba memory model follows vLLM's source but has not been checked
  against a boot.

<!-- /findings:setup -->

- Engine: vLLM v0.29.0 in one pinned runner image (digest above).
- Each boot: download weights to the pod volume, verify every file, start
  vLLM, read its memory profiling lines, run the task suite, run the
  serving benchmark, tear the pod down. A watchdog outside the run
  terminated nothing: every pod ended with its run.
- Scoring: exact match after whitespace normalization. Phase 1b also
  ignores a trailing full stop ("Paris." answers "just the city name").
  Every recorded answer was re-scored under the Phase 1b rule without a
  new generation; each re-score is its own record, linked to the answer it
  re-scores.
- Cost: what the ledger tracked per pod, reconciled against RunPod's own
  bill for the same window.

Repeat boots of one solution bound the measurement noise:

<!-- findings:repeats -->
| Model | GPU | Boots | Weights spread % | KV spread % | Activation spread % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
<!-- /findings:repeats -->

Those run-time predictions were wrong in four ways, all found by comparing
them with these boots and all fixed in the calculator since:

- a tied output projection counted twice (Qwen3-1.7B, +17%);
- without an index file, only the first dtype of a checkpoint counted
  (Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 lost its FP8 layers, -22%);
- whole-model bytes compared with vLLM's per-GPU figure (tensor parallel 2,
  +100%);
- activation estimated as 10% of the weights. The profiled peak does not
  follow the weights: Qwen3-8B and its GPTQ copy, a third of the size,
  both measured 1.19 GiB. It follows the output projection (vocabulary x
  hidden size) plus a small per-token term.

## Failures and fixes

One broken plan per failure class. Apron diagnosed the error from the log,
changed the plan itself, booted it again and re-ran the task suite and the
serving measurement.

<!-- findings:fixes -->
| Class | Broken plan | vLLM source | Diagnosis | Change | Restart | Request | Label | Record |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 oom_weight_load | Qwen/Qwen3-14B on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `model_executor/layers/linear.py:192` | oom_weight_load | resource_allocation.gpu_sku: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 → NVIDIA RTX A6000 | verified | satisfied | Fixed | `1220f4b5d596eaa3` |
| 2 oom_kv_cache | Qwen/Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:879` | oom_kv_cache | engine_configuration.max_model_len: 40960 → 32640 | verified | satisfied | Fixed | `1220e8f6ea8e7da0` |
| 3 max_model_len | mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `config/model.py:2502` | max_model_len | engine_configuration.max_model_len: 999999 → 32768 | verified | satisfied | Fixed | `12207f1e236c341a` |
| 4 dtype_incompatible | google/gemma-2-2b-it on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `config/model.py:2262` | dtype_incompatible | dtype: float16 → bfloat16 | verified | satisfied | Fixed | `122038df2ccafa66` |
| 5 tp_divisibility | Qwen/Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB | `config/model.py:1414` | tp_divisibility | tensor_parallel: 3 → 2 | verified | satisfied | Fixed | `12208faa3f0af819` |
| 6 quant_compute_capability | ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3-0.6B-FPQuant-RTN-MXFP4 on NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 | `config/vllm.py:791` | quant_compute_capability | resource_allocation.model_id: ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3-0.6B-FPQuant-RTN-MXFP4 → Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 | verified | violated | Alternative with trade-offs | `122006d6b9842e80` |
<!-- /findings:fixes -->

Class 6 took two attempts.

- The broken plan asked for a model quantized with `fp_quant` on an H100.
  vLLM refused: the method needs compute capability 10.0.
- The first fix moved the plan to a B200. The capability check passed; the
  weights then failed to load (`backward_hadamard_matrix`: no parameter of
  that name). vLLM removed that parameter as dead code in
  vllm-project/vllm#44122 (v0.23.0), and all 32 FPQuant checkpoints on the
  Hub still store it. No GPU can load them on v0.29.0.
- The second fix keeps the H100 and serves the same network in a format the
  H100 runs. Apron proposed the original model, confirmed it on the Hub
  (same architecture, same final-norm weights), and chose
  `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8` from the checkpoints the Hub lists as quantized
  from it. One listed "quantized" checkpoint was a fine-tune; its weights
  gave it away and it was dropped.
- It booted and served, and answered one of three questions (2 + 2 → "2").
  Mechanism verified, request violated: an alternative with trade-offs, not
  a fix. Whether the misses come from FP8 or from the model's size is not
  measured yet.

The B200 boot ($1.39) failed in a way the checkpoint's own file headers
could have shown for free. Apron now reads the tensor names before paying
for a boot and refuses a checkpoint the pinned engine would not load.

## How to reproduce

```bash
uv run python scripts/cohort_findings.py --check
APRON_COHORT_GATE=1 uv run pytest tests/test_exit_gate_1b_cohort.py -m cohort
```

Every digest in the tables resolves to a record under
`_dev_notes/cohort-run/records/`; the record store accepts a digest prefix.

## What's next

Which models or GPUs should be measured next? The command-line tool and
public record releases are not ready yet.
